Constraints
* Please add a constraint on the length of [[phrase]].

Cases
* Validator 4: Please remove the trailing newline from the input.

* Validator 3: "Squash" and "squish" have "u" as their first vowel, not "a", "i" or "o".

* The combination a + o appears in Validators 4 and 5, but not in any of the visible tests.

Thanks.

G'day fellow Australian,
Nice puzzle. I do think it would be better to provide a brief description of the task rather than a link to wikipedia. The link could still be included alongside a description. For your list of examples, it could be reduced to 4 phrases, 1 for each of length 2 and 3 and separators ' ' and '-'.

Input
 - Change to: <<1 Line:>> A string of {{2}} or {{3}} words, separated by spaces or {{-}}.

Output
 - Change to: <<1 Line:>> The string after sorting the words, with the same separator as the input string.

Constraints
 - Change line 2 to "Input is always either {{2}} or {{3}} words."

Cases
 - More space separated case pairs would be good
 - More 3 word long case pairs would be good. I'm thinking 1 where the output is the input reversed, 2 or 3 where 2 words are swapped, 1 where no change is made.
 - bing-bang-boom would probably be a good validator for tic-tac-toe, even better if you can think of other phrases that are better matches.

Thanks, sorry this was meant to be private for now.
I'm not sure if you'll see this comment as I have now moved it to private, but I'll reply again when I move it to WIP if not.

Thanks for spotting these, as always. :)

Implemented all but the length line, seems unnecessary (only C langs would care, and their stub tells them anyway?), I like clashes with minimal text.

Constraints
* I see your point, and it's true that the stub already conveys this. However, beginners might not immediately understand that implication, and the stub shouldn't replace an explicit statement of the constraint. So I'd still suggest adding it, though of course the final decision is yours.

Cases
* The combination a + o now appears in Validator 5 only. I'm not sure if my previous comment was misunderstood. I think these input phrases are fine and shouldn't be removed; instead, they should be redistributed so that the combination appears in both tests and validators.

Thanks.
Ok, thanks for the feedback, implemented now. :)

Looks good. I was thinking yesterday that reverse mode would be good, especially with the stub generator statement, so I'm glad you've turned it on.
The hyphens in the statement should be formatted as constants. I think doing the same for the words "spaces" and "hyphens" would be nice, but it's not as important.
Really doesn't matter, but there's no 3 word space-separated strings. I'd just choose an existing pair of strings (1 test, 1 validator) and replace the hyphens.
Add a constraint for [[n]]: {{1}}≤ [[n]]≤ {{10}}

Fun puzzle 👍
All done, thanks for the great feedback.
